title: RTK Query Cache Identity and Invalidation Checkpoint

questions.prompt: The final subscriber leaves at t=40s with keepUnusedDataFor: 60. No one returns. When is eviction expected?

options.label: Around t=100s, because retention starts after the final unsubscribe.
At t=60s measured from the original request.
Never, because only mutations remove query entries.

questions.explanation: Unused retention starts when the subscription count reaches zero. It is not measured from fetch time, and cache eviction does not require a mutation.

questions.prompt: Deleting a record on page one shifts page three, which never provided that record tag. What helps?

options.label: Invalidate only the deleted record ID, which always matches all pages.
Increase keepUnusedDataFor so the stale page lives longer.
Invalidate a scoped collection or PARTIAL-LIST tag as well as relevant entity tags.

questions.explanation: A collection dependency covers membership/count changes outside a visible page. An unprovided entity tag will not match that page, and longer retention cannot correct stale membership.

questions.prompt: Tenant changes affect only prepareHeaders; the endpoint arguments stay equal. What is missing?

options.label: A random number in every argument to disable all reuse.
Explicit cache scope and account-transition cleanup for identity-dependent data.
Nothing: all request headers automatically enter the default key.

questions.explanation: Headers are not automatically default key dimensions. Model non-secret identity scope and clear protected state on transition; random keys waste reuse and fail to express the actual data contract.

questions.prompt: A matching tag is invalidated for an entry with no active subscribers. What normally happens?

options.label: The unused matching entry is removed.
It must immediately refetch despite having no subscribers.
Its JSON data is automatically patched from the mutation result.

questions.explanation: Invalidation removes unused matches and refetches subscribed matches. Tags neither force background fetches for every unused entry nor automatically merge mutation data into query responses.

questions.prompt: A mutation succeeds but delayed invalidation never runs while a queryFn stays pending. What should you inspect?

options.label: Only CSS, because a successful mutation guarantees immediate refresh.
Whether the same string tag exists in a different API slice.
Pending work and the API invalidation policy; make the query lifecycle settle appropriately.

questions.explanation: RTK 2.x delayed invalidation waits for pending work to settle. Styling cannot unblock the lifecycle, and matching tag names in separate API slices do not share invalidation.

questions.prompt: Why should an empty author list still provide a collection tag?

options.label: Because collection tags globally normalize all author objects.
A later create can invalidate the cached empty collection.
Because an empty list otherwise becomes a mutation.

questions.explanation: An empty result is still a cached server projection that can become stale after creation. Tags do not change endpoint type and do not provide global entity normalization.
